profile.reading:
This is Atlas Power's cryptocurrency mining and high-density computing campus on a 77-acre site in Judson Township, west of Williston, in Williams County, North Dakota. The project was announced in January 2022 by Atlas Power Holdings (ND), LLC, developed locally by FX Solutions Inc. of Missoula, Montana, with North Dakota's governor's office touting it at announcement as one of the largest data centers of its kind, tied to roughly $1.9 billion in planned investment. The build was structured in three phases: an initial Phase 1 of 240 megawatts across 16 buildings, each 350 feet by 30 feet, housing tens of thousands of servers; a Phase 2 expansion toward 500 megawatts; and a Phase 3 target of 700 megawatts. That 700-megawatt figure is the phase-three ceiling stated at the original 2022 announcement, not a confirmed operating capacity, and no operator disclosure of capacity actually energized has been found publicly. Power is supplied by Mountrail-Williams Electric Cooperative. State officials projected more than 30 permanent jobs and over 100 construction jobs across a roughly two-year build.

The facility's public record includes a documented regulatory dispute with Williams County. Beginning in April 2023, county staff responding to resident noise complaints found that eight Phase 2 buildings were operating without the required Certificate of Occupancy and identified building-code and zoning violations; the county's Board of Commissioners gave Atlas Power 45 days to correct the issues in May 2023. When the county determined in June 2023 that the violations had not been fully resolved, it directed Mountrail-Williams Electric Cooperative to disconnect power to the affected buildings under county building-code authority; the cooperative instead filed a petition for declaratory judgment against the county and did not carry out the disconnection. By June 29, 2023, county officials confirmed the code violations had been corrected, required state and county inspections had been met, and Atlas Power had paid $232,000 in fines, at which point the county approved a 60-day temporary Certificate of Occupancy, pending completion of acoustical panels, security fencing, and a required emergency access road before a full Certificate of Occupancy would be considered.

As a Bitcoin-mining and high-density hosting operation rather than a commercial colocation facility, Atlas Power does not publish a leasing spec sheet; its business is running its own compute at scale near low-cost regional power rather than marketing rack space to outside tenants. The public record here -- state and county government sources rather than the operator's own disclosures -- is what documents the facility's real scale and its friction with local zoning and noise rules during buildout, a more informative record in practice than any marketing page would be.

compliance_history.event: Williams County began receiving noise complaints from residents around the site; county staff identified building code and zoning ordinance violations while responding, and determined that eight Phase 2 buildings were operating without the required Certificate of Occupancy.
The Board of County Commissioners gave Atlas Power 45 days to rectify the identified violations.

Told the May order had not been fully addressed, the Board directed Mountrail-Williams Electric Cooperative to disconnect power to buildings on the Phase 2 permit, under the authority of the county building code.
MWEC served a Petition for Declaratory Judgment on the county and did not comply with the disconnection directive.

The Board unanimously approved a standard 60-day Temporary Certificate of Occupancy after officials confirmed the code violations were rectified, state and county inspection requirements met, and $232,000 in fines paid. A full Certificate of Occupancy was to be considered after acoustical panels, security fencing and a required emergency access road were completed.

reading: Atlas Power is a privately held data center developer headquartered in Butte, Montana, founded and led by Kevin Washington as founder and president. The company's flagship project is a large crypto mining and high-performance computing campus in Williston, North Dakota, in Williams County within the Bakken oil patch, built by contractor FX Solutions Inc. under president Richard Tabish, with Atlas Power taking ownership and operation once construction phases complete. North Dakota's governor's office described the project as a 1.9 billion dollar multiyear investment scaling in three phases, from 240 megawatts in the first phase to 500 megawatts in a second phase and 700 megawatts in a third, with sitework beginning in January 2022 and an approximately two-year construction timeline for early phases. The facility is designed around access to low cost regional power, including associated natural gas from oil production in the Bakken formation, an increasingly common power sourcing pattern for large computing loads sited in oil and gas producing regions. State officials projected more than 100 construction jobs during buildout and more than 30 permanent operational positions once running. As a large-scale, power-driven crypto mining and HPC campus in a resource region rather than a traditional metro colocation market, Atlas Power's profile in this registry resembles other power-focused developers rather than the metro wholesale and hyperscale campuses concentrated in Northern Virginia, Texas, and similar established markets.
